title: Hauntings & Unexplained Phenomena / Dream Guidance
byline: Coast to Coast AM Staff - October 11, 2026
excerpt: Paranormal investigator Colin Browen recounted chilling childhood hauntings, mysterious entities, and terrifying encounters during investigations. Followed by Dr. Bonnie Buckner on Mall World, shared dreaming, collective consciousness, and dreams' potential for personal transformation.
content:
Guest host Ryan Wrecker (email) was joined by filmmaker and paranormal investigator Colin Browen, who discussed his experiences investigating alleged hauntings and unexplained phenomena, including frightening encounters in his childhood home in South Dakota. Although it was newly constructed, the family reported numerous disturbing incidents, including unexplained crying, apparent doppelgangers, and an encounter with a shadowy figure he later identified with the Hat Man folklore. Browen recalled how these experiences affected his entire family and how attempts by three psychics to cleanse the property seemingly made matters worse. He speculated that an entity may have attached itself to his family during a period of grief and trauma, noting that family members continue to report unusual experiences despite living in different states. Although he believes most spirits are not malicious, Browen maintained that genuinely negative entities exist and can be difficult to remove.

Browen also described some of his most memorable paranormal investigations, emphasizing the importance of researching a location's history and ruling out conventional explanations for unusual activity. He recalled recently detecting unexplained cigar smoke at a reportedly haunted West Virginia hotel, an experience that paralleled host Ryan Wrecker's sudden detection of cigarette smoke during the interview. Browen then recounted a particularly disturbing investigation of a South Dakota family's home, where residents claimed to have contacted an entity called Zozo through a Ouija board. During the investigation, he saw dogs growling at an unseen presence and a door slam inexplicably. Later, a review of infrared footage revealed what appeared to be a woman in white. Although the original episode was later removed from YouTube, Browen said the experience remains among his most compelling encounters. He acknowledged that most paranormal investigations involve long periods of inactivity, but occasional extraordinary experiences continue to motivate his work.

------------------------------------------

During the second half of the show, psychologist and dreamwork expert Bonnie Buckner, PhD, explored the phenomenon known as "Mall World," in which people report recurring dreams of seemingly similar shopping malls. She traced the phenomenon to a 2021 Reddit discussion that inspired others to share their experiences and even draw maps of their dream locations. While some interpret these similarities as evidence of shared dreaming or collective consciousness, Buckner suggested that malls are familiar cultural environments, much like schools and airports, that naturally appear in dreams. She explained that these settings can reflect emotional states, personal experiences, and societal attitudes. Some dreamers encounter crowded spaces, while others experience eerie, empty corridors. Buckner also discussed what she calls the "dream field," suggesting that people may be connected through thoughts and emotions beyond their immediate awareness.

Buckner described dream incubation, a practice of setting intentions before sleep to explore questions, encourage lucid dreaming, or potentially share dream experiences with others. She recounted exercises in which participants reported meeting in dreams and subsequently comparing details they believed verified their shared experiences. Emphasizing that dreaming is an active cognitive process, she explained how dreams can foster creativity, help regulate emotions, and reveal insights that might otherwise go unnoticed. Buckner also delved into research from her institute and Sofia University, reporting that participants in a 10-week dreamwork study experienced fewer nightmares, less distress, and greater well-being and personal agency. She encouraged listeners to approach dreams with curiosity, recognize their potential for personal transformation, and remain open to mysteries science has yet to explain fully.
